mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a true characteristic of ants?

options.A: Ants have a segmented body with head, thorax, and abdomen.
options.B: Ants have wings throughout their life.
options.D: Ants live in colonies with a queen.

mcqs.answer: Ants have wings throughout their life.
mcqs.explanation: Ants only develop wings during the reproductive phase (winged males and queens). Worker ants are wingless for their entire lives. Therefore option B is the misconception. Options A, C and D correctly describe ant characteristics: a segmented body, pheromone communication, and colony living with a queen.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand division of work in an ant colony
mcqs.question: Why does division of labor make an ant colony more successful?

options.A: All ants perform the same tasks, ensuring flexibility.
options.B: Specialized roles allow efficient gathering of food, caring for brood, and defending the nest.
options.C: Only the queen does all work, so other ants rest.
options.D: Division of work leads to chaos because ants cannot coordinate.

mcqs.answer: Specialized roles allow efficient gathering of food, caring for brood, and defending the nest.
mcqs.explanation: In ant colonies, workers, soldiers, and the queen each have specific duties. This specialization speeds up food collection, brood care, and defense, enhancing colony survival. Option B correctly captures this benefit. Options A and C are false because ants are not identical in function, and the queen’s role is limited to reproduction. Option D misrepresents the coordinated nature of ant societies.

mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the cooperative behavior of ants with that of another social insect?

options.A: Ants cooperate only when foraging, while bees cooperate only in building hives.
options.B: Ants exhibit cooperative behavior in tasks like carrying large prey together, similar to termites building mounds.
options.C: Ants never cooperate; they are solitary insects.
options.D: Ants cooperate by sharing food through direct feeding, unlike any other insects.

mcqs.answer: Ants exhibit cooperative behavior in tasks like carrying large prey together, similar to termites building mounds.
mcqs.explanation: Ants often work together to transport items larger than an individual can carry, showing clear cooperation. This is comparable to termites that collectively construct complex mounds. Option B correctly highlights a parallel. Option A is inaccurate because ants also cooperate in nest building and defense, and bees cooperate in many activities beyond hive construction. Option C is false; ants are highly social. Option D misstates ant feeding behavior; while trophallaxis occurs, many insects share food, so the claim of uniqueness is incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify different roles within a colony
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an ant caste with its primary function?
mcqs.explanation: The queen ant’s main role is reproduction; she lays all the eggs for the colony. Workers handle foraging and nest maintenance, soldiers protect the colony, and drones (if present) are males whose primary purpose is to mate with queens, not defense. Therefore, option C is the accurate pairing. Options A, B, and D incorrectly assign functions to the respective castes.
